analyst_view.overall: Bournemouth (8th) arrive on a seven-game winning run in all competitions, and one preview says they are chasing a club-record fourth straight Premier League clean sheet. Marco Rose rotated heavily for Thursday's 3-1 win at Sparta Prague and is expected to bring back his first XI, though he admitted 'Ipswich away is not easy' and his side have won only one of four league away games. Gary O'Neil's Ipswich (14th) are winless in three league games but have one of the league's better attacks, and Sasa Lukic may return from a groin injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. Ipswich have scored freely, with 14 league goals and two recent comebacks from behind, and Bournemouth's front four of Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier and Evanilson return fresh. But Bournemouth have conceded only once in their last six, which balances things out, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Bournemouth's wide players return and Ipswich should push forward at home through Fatawu and Philogene. Nothing in the news moves us clearly away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, already a high figure, with Simon Hooper refereeing. Neither side has suspension or discipline issues in the news, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. A full-strength Bournemouth attack against an Ipswich side that likes to attack at Portman Road fits the model's busy total. We have nothing to add either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Bournemouth's first-choice attack led by Evanilson comes back in after being rested in Prague, where even the rotated side was busy in front of goal. Ipswich, with Emersonn up front and creative players like Enciso, should also test Petrovic.
